euronews.title: Uzbekistan's poverty rate falls as World Bank highlights role of wages and employment
euronews.description: The Bank estimates that the national rate fell from 17% in 2021 to 5.8% in 2025, with 3.7 million people moving above the threshold. The government separately reports 3.6% for the first nine months of 2026.

euronews.title: Milei and Sánchez exchange a cold greeting at Ibero-American Summit

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, grève du 5 novembre : entre 600 000 et 1,6 million de manifestants en France jeudi, une « conférence sociale » avec les syndicats et le patronat prévue à Matignon lundi
lemonde.description: La CGT estime que les mobilisations ont réuni près de 1,6 million de personnes, dont 350 000 à Paris. Peu avant 17 heures, Beauvau a fait savoir que près de 600 000 personnes ont participé à la mobilisation, ajoutant qu’il s’agissait d’une estimation non définitive.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, midterms 2026 : les dernières informations après la débâcle électorale de Trump et des républicains
lemonde.description: Le Monde tient un direct consacré aux midterms, les élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis, où les démocrates ont signé une victoire sans appel avec une majorité acquise aux deux chambres du Congrès américain.

lemonde.title: Sébastien Lecornu exhorte les banques à financer les candidats à l’élection présidentielle
lemonde.description: Le premier ministre a envoyé deux nouveaux courriers aux banques françaises. Celles-ci plaident pour une solution impliquant des établissements financiers détenus directement ou indirectement par l’Etat.

lemonde.title: Dépenses du gouvernement : une étude relève « l’opacité » des rémunérations dans les cabinets ministériels
lemonde.description: Dans une note pour l’Observatoire de l’éthique publique, qu’il préside, l’ancien député René Dosière évalue le « coût du gouvernement Lecornu » à 165,7 millions d’euros en année pleine, soit moins d’un millième des dépenses publiques.

lemonde.title: Sahara occidental : « L’échec de la diplomatie risque de renforcer la frange du Front Polisario favorable à l’escalade militaire avec le Maroc »
lemonde.description: L’analyste Riccardo Fabiani explique, dans un entretien au « Monde », que le retrait de la mission onusienne de maintien de la paix dans le territoire sahraoui, le 1ᵉʳ novembre, pourrait se traduire sur le terrain par une dégradation de la situation sécuritaire.

lemonde.title: Guillaume de Tonquédec, seul en scène et émouvant dans « Ta mère et moi »
lemonde.description: Le comédien, tout en retenue et profondeur, nous chavire dans l’adaptation à la scène de son livre consacré à ses parents, Marie-Christine et Patrick, portée par une scénographie inventive.

lemonde.title: Ce que l’on sait des alertes à la bombe qui ont perturbé le trafic aérien en Europe
lemonde.description: A midi jeudi, douze vols avaient été visés par des alertes à la bombe, ont signalé plusieurs autorités et compagnies. Tous les vols se sont posés en sécurité, ont-elles confirmé.

lemonde.title: Paraguay : le président Santiago Peña annonce sa démission
lemonde.description: L’annonce intervient quarante-huit heures après l’éclatement d’une crise bancaire, qui a vu la Banque centrale du Paraguay mettre sous tutelle Ueno, une entité financière revendiquant 2,94 millions de clients, dont les dépôts ont été gelés temporairement.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : depuis la Maison Blanche, Melania Trump appelle à un cessez-le-feu « durable » en Ukraine
lemonde.description: « Nous devons désormais faire preuve du courage que nous avons montré à Olechky pour trouver un terrain d’entente. Ensemble, nous pouvons bâtir quelque chose de plus durable qu’un simple cessez-le-feu temporaire », a déclaré l’épouse du président américain, que la Maison Blanche met en avant depuis plusieurs semaines dans les efforts de médiation entre la Russie et l’Ukraine.

lemonde.title: Herbert Blomstedt, légendaire chef d’orchestre suédois qui dirigeait toujours à près de 100 ans, est mort
lemonde.description: Durant sa carrière internationale d’une durée exceptionnelle, il a marqué les esprits par son sens de la précision et son humilité. Il s’est éteint le 4 novembre, à 99 ans.

lemonde.title: Dette : les députés veulent mettre fin aux emprunts d’Etat indexés sur l’inflation
lemonde.description: Avec la forte hausse des prix, l’Etat doit payer des intérêts très élevés aux détenteurs d’obligations indexées. Le mécanisme risque de lui coûter plus de 10 milliards d’euros en 2026. Une majorité de députés a demandé, mercredi 4 novembre, la fin de ce système.

lemonde.title: Rénovation des lycées : la liste du gouvernement contestée par les régions, qui dénoncent une méthode « inacceptable »
lemonde.description: Lundi, le ministre de l’éducation nationale, Edouard Geffray, a annoncé que la plateforme de concertation avait permis d’identifier 200 bâtiments à rénover en priorité, se félicitant que, « pour la première fois, les lycéens ont un effet sur leur vie ».

lemonde.title: Antonio Ferrara, figure française du grand banditisme, condamné à treize ans de prison en Belgique
lemonde.description: Avec neuf coprévenus, il était poursuivi pour avoir planifié l’attaque à main armée d’un centre-fort à Bochum, en Allemagne.

lemonde.title: Cristiano Ronaldo prend sa retraite internationale, triste fin d’une histoire qui a un peu trop duré
lemonde.description: Le footballeur portugais a annoncé qu’il raccrochait les crampons en sélection, jeudi, dans une vidéo publiée sur Instagram. Véritable légende dans son pays, il part sur un coup d’éclat et une séparation précipitée de la Seleçao das Quinas, le 30 septembre.

lemonde.title: Avec « Muse », John Legend et Pharell Williams font revivre l’esprit du jazz : « Nous avons beaucoup pensé à Nina Simone pendant l’enregistrement »
lemonde.description: Inspirés par la chanteuse afro-américaine, les grands orchestres de jazz et le hip-hop, le pianiste et le producteur ont enregistré leur album à Paris, dans les locaux de Louis Vuitton.

lemonde.title: Sur Netflix, une deuxième saison du tonnerre pour les espions de « Black Doves »
lemonde.description: Keira Knightley et Ben Whishaw rappellent toute l’étendue de leur talent dans la nouvelle saison de la série créée par Joe Barton.

rfi.title: Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding
rfi.description: Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.

rfi.title: ‘We’ll get them’: Macron’s private comments on rivals revealed in new book
rfi.description: Private messages exchanged between French President Emmanuel Macron and journalist Françoise Degois over two years have been published in a new book, revealing his views on political rivals, the rise of the far right and his own leadership. The president reportedly learnt of the book’s existence just three days before its release.

rfi.title: Unicef warns attacks on water supply in conflict zones have tripled in five years
rfi.description: Attacks damaging or destroying water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, Unicef warned on Thursday, leaving millions of children increasingly exposed to disease, malnutrition and violence.

rfi.title: Republican losses show Trump is 'not necessarily the best person to latch on to'
rfi.description: The Democrats’ takeover of the United States Congress sets the stage for a showdown with President Donald Trump, but is unlikely to change his approach to foreign affairs, including the war with Iran, says political scientist Eduardo Gamarra. Speaking to RFI, the Florida International University professor says the party now faces a choice: whether to spend their time investigating the president, or seek compromises on the country’s most pressing problems.

rfi.title: French prosecutors investigate €100m cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel banking group
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.

rfi.title: MPs unanimously reject 2027 French budget as political deadlock continues
rfi.description: France's National Assembly has overwhelmingly rejected the government's draft budget for 2027 after MPs from across the political spectrum voted against a heavily amended version of the legislation, sending the bill to the Senate in its original form and setting the stage for another round of difficult negotiations.

rfi.title: Corruption in Kenya taking massive toll on economic growth, warns World Bank
rfi.description: Corruption is costing Kenya billions of dollars each year in lost revenue, inflated business costs, and lost earnings for workers, while taking a huge toll on investment and economic growth, the World Bank said in a report published Wednesday.

rfi.title: South Africa votes in local elections as growing anger threatens ANC

rfi.title: Nine out of 10 crimes against journalists go unpunished, Unesco says
rfi.description: Monday marks the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists – chosen in memory of Ghislaine Dupont and Claude Verlon, two journalists from Radio France Internationale who were murdered in Mali on 2 November, 2013. According to a report by Unesco, attacks and harassment targeting the press continue to go largely unpunished in Africa and across the globe.

france24fr.title: Manifestations contre la vie chère en France : le taux de pauvreté au plus haut
france24fr.description: En France, le taux de pauvreté n’a jamais été aussi haut depuis au moins trente ans. Une situation qui fait partie des enjeux au cœur des mobilisations de ce jeudi 5 novembre. La France comptait 9,8 millions de personnes sous le seuil de pauvreté en 2024 selon l'Insee. Environ 15,5 % de la population française vit chaque mois avec moins de 60 % du revenu médian, soit moins de 1 337 euros pour une personne seule. Les précisions de Ludovic De Foucaud, journaliste à France 24.

france24fr.title: Midterms : le vice-président américain prend ses distances avec Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Le vice-président américain J.D. Vance a pris ⁠mercredi 4 novembre ses distances ​avec la guerre en Iran menée par le président Donald Trump, s'interrogeant sur la pertinence d'une telle décision et imputant au conflit les lourds ​revers subis la veille par les républicains lors des élections de mi-mandat au Congrès. Les précisions de Matthieu Mabin, chroniqueur international à France 24.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : le consensus pro-israélien de l'opinion américaine se fissure
france24fr.description: La victoire du progressiste Abdul El-Sayed aux élections de mi-mandat, après une campagne marquée par ses critiques d'Israël, illustre l'érosion du soutien de l'opinion américaine à l'État hébreu depuis les guerres à Gaza et en Iran. Entre coût de la vie liées aux tensions au Moyen-Orient et aspirations isolationnistes à droite, l'alignement historique des États-Unis sur le gouvernement israélien vacille aussi.

france24fr.title: JOJ : match fou entre le Sénégal et le Panama en futsal
france24fr.description: Les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse se poursuivent au Sénégal. L'équipe masculine du pays hôte ont créé la sensation en futsal face au Panama. Notre correspondante Sarah Sakho revient sur cette folle rencontre et nous donne les autres temps forts de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Budget 2027 : l'Assemblée nationale rejette à l'unanimité le projet de budget de l'État
france24fr.description: Les députés ont rejeté mercredi 4 novembre en première lecture, et à l'unanimité des votes exprimés, le projet de budget de l'Etat 2027, qui sera donc envoyé dans sa version initiale au Sénat. Après avoir supprimé plusieurs articles-clés du texte gouvernemental, l'Assemblée a rejeté comme l'an dernier la partie "recettes" du texte, avec 458 voix contre, issues de tous les groupes, et deux abstentions au sein du groupe communiste et ultramarin.

france24fr.title: Grèves en France : comment les manifestations sont vues de l'étranger ?
france24fr.description: Les mobilisations aux luttes convergentes s'enchaînent en France depuis des semaines, dépassant parfois les frontières de la France. En Europe, la jeunesse albanaise, italienne et grecque est, elle aussi, sortie dans les rues. À l'échelle internationale, comment ces manifestations sont -elles vues ? Peuvent-elles créer un effet boule de neige ?  Les précisions d'Alberto Toscano, journaliste et écrivain italien.

france24fr.title: Grève du 5 novembre : plus de 9,8 millions de Français sous le seuil de pauvreté
france24fr.description: Le pouvoir d'achat et la précarité sont aussi les luttes portées lors de ce jeudi 5 novembre, journée de grève intersyndicale. En France, selon l'Insee, 9.8 % des Français sont sous le seuil de pauvreté (2024). Une justice sociale est demandée, en solution, les manifestants proposent notamment la taxation des ultra-riches. Le Secours populaire, affirme lui que 26 % des Français estiment être en situation de précarité.

france24fr.title: Chris Pappas aux Midterms : le premier sénateur ouvertement gay, un non-sujet lors de sa campagne
france24fr.description: Chris Pappas, élu dans le New Hampshire lors des midterms le mardi 3 novembre, devient le premier sénateur ouvertement gay. Après sa victoire, il est apparu avec celui qu'il décrit comme "son mari fantastique". Son homosexualité n'a jamais été un sujet de débat lors de sa campagne, où il a abordé les thématiques qui inquiétaient les citoyens du New Hampshire. Les explications de James André, grand reporter à France 24.

france24fr.title: La déroute du camp Trump aux midterms : qu'en est-il de la future politique économique ?
france24fr.description: Suite à la défaite du camp Trump ce mardi 3 novembre aux midterms, des questionnements quant au futur économique du pays émergent. Moins d'investissement dans le militaire, plus dans la santé et la taxation des ultras-riches sont parmis les requêtes des démocrates : le budget devra lui, être bouclé le 11 décembre et promet de grands débats. Les précisions d'Ali Laïdi, chroniqueur intelligence économique de France 24.

france24fr.title: Grève du 5 novembre  : une augmentation du SMIC demandée pas les syndicats
france24fr.description: Déjà un "succès" de la mobilisation du jeudi 5 novembre pour les syndicats : les grèves pour différentes causes sociales avaient rassemblé à la mi-journée des centaines de milliers de personnes hors région parisienne, mettant le gouvernement sous pression pour concéder une hausse importante du SMIC et la suppression de Parcoursup entre autres. Les explications de Marc Perelman, chroniqueur politique à France 24.

france24fr.title: Grève du 5 novembre : le cortège devrait rassembler entre 40 000 et 80 000 manifestants à Paris
france24fr.description: Près de 10 %, des agents de la fonction publique d'Etat ont participé jeudi 5 novembre au mouvement de grève dans le cadre de la journée d'action pour les salaires et le pouvoir d'achat, d'après le ministère de l'Action et des Comptes publics. france24fr.title: Midterms : la déroute républicaine fragilise l'avenir de Pete Hegseth au Pentagone

observador.description: A comunicação de Montenegro ao País sobre habitação, o puxão de orelhas de António José Seguro e a mudança de estratégia do Governo sobre as acampadas foram os temas da Vichyssoise desta semana.

observador.title: Russell Brand condenado por violação e agressões sexuais
observador.description: O ator manteve uma cara "sem emoções" ao ouvir o veredicto, mas repetiu "estou bem" à equipa legal. Pena de prisão considerada "óbvia" pelo juiz, mas sentença só será conhecida segunda-feira.

observador.title: Nuno Melo relativiza ataque informático a telemóvel
observador.description: Nuno Melo defendeu que divulgou o caso com objetivo "pedagógico" e que outros países como Espanha, EUA e Países Baixos já viram governantes atacados.

observador.title: Eurodeputado questiona Bruxelas sobre renovação de licenças
observador.description: A proposta da Anacom para a renovação de licenças móveis já chegou a Bruxelas. Eurodeputado português questionou a Comissão Europeia sobre as extensões propostas, revelando a sua preocupação.

observador.title: Alertas para chuva já esta sexta. Mas o pior chegará segunda
observador.description: Os avisos amarelos desta sexta-feira são só o começo: vem aí uma sucessão de depressões, chuva forte e vento. Não há nada no Atlântico que não pareça vir até cá. Mas os ventos vão aquecer as noites.

observador.title: PSP não vê "indisciplina" em polícias com cravos na farda
observador.description: PSP descarta "comportamento incorreto" em agentes com cravos na farda. Já as multas por buzinar, que "não iam voltar a acontecer", repetiram-se.

observador.title: Presidente do Paraguai demite-se após ameaça de destituição
observador.description: A crise política foi desencadeada pela intervenção no Ueno Bank, uma instituição financeira à qual o chefe de Estado tem sido associado e que recebeu recursos financeiros de entidades públicas.

observador.title: As notícias das 17h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: "Basta que sejas perfeita para que gostem de ti"
observador.description: Há pais e mães que dão a entender a um filho que o amor se ganha com a perfeição. O que acontece a uma criança que aprende que só é amada se não falhar?

observador.title: Sindicato da polícia critica ministra da Justiça
observador.description: O SINAPOL rejeitou a equiparação feita por Rita Alarcão Júdice entre manifestantes e polícias nos protestos pela habitação. "Quem ataca e quem se defende não estão na mesma posição."

observador.title: Timing, JJ, Mendes. Como é que Ronaldo chegou aqui?
observador.description: O adeus precipitou-se com a colisão com Jorge Jesus, mas a montanha-russa começou no Qatar e na ausência de Jorge Mendes. Em meses, o impensável apressou-se. Mas como é que Ronaldo chegou aqui?

observador.title: Regras para IA: e se eu for prejudicado?
observador.description: Se uma pessoa for prejudicada por um conteúdo gerado por Inteligência Artificial, como prova o nexo de causalidade quando nem os especialistas conseguem explicar o funcionamento do sistema?

observador.title: CGD lucra 1.434 milhões e dá mais 41% em crédito para casa
observador.description: O banco público terminou os primeiros nove meses do ano com lucros de 1.434 milhões, mais 2,5% do que no período homólogo. Banco aumentou em 41,2% a concessão de crédito à habitação.

observador.title: PS quer ouvir INE sobre estatísticas da população
observador.description: Socialistas consideram "bastante grave" a instabilidade nas estatísticas populacionais e querem ouvir a direção do INE após discussão do OE2027.

observador.title: Cimeira Ibero-Americana adota rede de redução de riscos
observador.description: Proposta portuguesa de rede ibero-americana de proteção civil foi aprovada, mas Argentina e Paraguai rejeitaram ainda pontos sobre IA e igualdade de género.

observador.title: Arsenio Dominguez cumpre segundo mandato na OMI até 2031
observador.description: O Conselho da OMI, reunido em Londres, decidiu prolongar por quatro anos o mandato do secretário-geral. Proposta segue para ratificação na Assembleia em 2027.

observador.title: Planet Fitness compra Be-Fit e entra em Portugal
observador.description: A gigante norte-americana dos ginásios entra em Portugal com 80.000 sócios e 25 clubes. Os espaços Be-Fit vão adotar progressivamente a marca Planet Fitness.

spiegel.title: NSDAP-Kartei: So forschen Sie nach der Recherche im SPIEGEL-Archiv weiter
spiegel.description: Sie haben die NSDAP-Kartei des SPIEGEL genutzt und fragen sich: Wie forsche ich weiter? Ab 19.30 Uhr beantworten Historiker Johannes Spohr und SPIEGEL-Redakteur Frederik Seeler Ihre Fragen im Livestream.

spiegel.title: Alan Jones ist tot: Nachruf auf den Formel-1-Weltmeister
spiegel.description: Alan Jones fuhr den Williams-Rennstall zum ersten WM-Titel in der Formel 1. Der Australier triumphierte in einem wilden Jahr des Motorsports. Mit 80 Jahren ist er nun gestorben.

spiegel.title: Midterms-Siege der Demokraten: Furcht vor KI-Regulierung lässt US-Tech-Aktien einbrechen
spiegel.description: Nach den US-Zwischenwahlen müssen sich KI-Konzerne wohl auf mehr politischen Gegenwind einstellen. Am Aktienmarkt verlieren deswegen nun die Werte von Chipherstellern deutlich an Wert – in den USA, aber auch in Deutschland.

spiegel.title: »White Tiger«: Wie Russland mutmaßlich Teenager für Anschläge rekrutiert
spiegel.description: Rekrutiert Russland Teenager im Netz, um Chaos zu verbreiten? Indizien legen das nahe: Brandanschläge, Messerattacken und ein Bündel Rubelscheine.

spiegel.title: Texas: Wie Gina Hinojosa die Republikaner-Hochburg umkrempeln will
spiegel.description: Gina Hinojosa ist für Texas noch wichtiger als der künftige Senator James Talarico: Die neue Gouverneurin will das Geflecht zwischen Republikanern und Oligarchen zerschlagen. Vor allem für Elon Musk könnte sich einiges ändern.

spiegel.title: Israel: Gadi Eisenkot bekommt die meisten Empfehlungen aus dem israelischen Parlament
spiegel.description: Israel sucht weiter nach einer Regierungskoalition. Jetzt haben sich die arabischen Parteien auf die Seite des Oppositionskandidaten geschlagen. Sicherheiten bringt das aber nicht.

spiegel.title: René Benko zu Zusatzstrafe von zwei Jahren verurteilt
spiegel.description: Im September wurde der frühere Signa-Chef zu zweieinhalb Jahren Haft verurteilt, nun kommen wegen Betrugs zwei zusätzliche Jahre zur Strafe dazu. Laut Gericht hat René Benko einen Investor um fünf Millionen Euro geschädigt.

spiegel.title: Haftbefehl: Rapper veröffentlicht Foto mit Verband auf der Nase
spiegel.description: Zuletzt kündigte der Manager von Haftbefehl eine längere Pause des Offenbacher Rappers an. Dann erschien ein neuer Song, nun kommt via Instagram ein Lebenszeichen. Mit Verband im Gesicht. Und persönlicher Botschaft.

spiegel.title: Janosch ist tot: So nehmen Autorinnen und Zeichner Abschied
spiegel.description: Der Tod des Kinderbuchkünstlers Janosch trifft auch Kolleginnen und Kollegen tief. Mit diesen Zeichnungen sagen einige Lebwohl.

spiegel.title: Bundesarbeitsgericht: Katholischer Verband durfte Angestellte nicht wegen Kirchenaustritt kündigen
spiegel.description: Mitarbeiter einer katholischen Einrichtung können bei einem Kirchenaustritt nicht automatisch entlassen werden. Zu dieser Entscheidung kam das Bundesarbeitsgericht im Fall einer Angestellten in einer Schwangerschaftsberatung.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Wann wird Ilse Aigner Bundespräsidentin-Kandidatin? Jürgen Klopps Kaderpolitik. Die 20 besten Bücher des Jahres
spiegel.description: Die Ilse-Aigner-Fans werden auch in der CDU immer lauter. Jürgen Klopp holt Niclas Füllkrug zurück. Und: Wir präsentieren die besten Bücher des Jahres. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

spiegel.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Nach Abreise-Posse erklärt er versöhnlich seinen Rücktritt
spiegel.description: Zuletzt reiste Cristiano Ronaldo beleidigt von seinem Team ab, jetzt überrascht der Stürmer mit einem fünfminütigen Video. Darin erklärt er sein Ende als Nationalspieler und bemüht sich um Versöhnung mit seinen Landsleuten.

spiegel.title: Fußball: Haftstrafe für Fan nach Ausschreitungen gegen Polizisten in Magdeburg
spiegel.description: Nach Ausschreitungen bei einem Zweitligaspiel muss ein Fußballfan ins Gefängnis. Die Staatsanwaltschaft hatte ihn sogar wegen versuchten Mords angeklagt. Einen Tötungsvorsatz sah das Gericht jedoch nicht.

spiegel.title: Hochtief: Baukonzern profitiert von KI-Boom - Gewinn um 40 Prozent gesteigert
spiegel.description: Der Baukonzern Hochtief jubelt über Rekordaufträge. Das liegt vor allem an KI-Rechenzentren in Asien, den USA und Europa, die dem Unternehmen Milliarden einbringen.

spiegel.title: Midterms: Donald Trump will, dass Dan Sullivan Dan Sullivans Stimmen bekommt
spiegel.description: Nun mischt der Präsident sich doch in die Auszählung ein: Donald Trumps wütet gegen die Wahl in Alaska, wo zwei fast namensgleiche Kandidaten antreten. Deren Stimmen sollten alle an einen der Kandidaten gehen, findet er.

spiegel.title: Hubert Aiwanger: Wie geht es nach dem Tod des Vizeregierungschefs in Bayern weiter?
spiegel.description: Trauerbeflaggung an staatlichen Dienstgebäuden in Bayern, im Münchner Prinz-Carl-Palais soll ein Kondolenzbuch ausgelegt werden: Der Tod von Hubert Aiwanger erschüttert. Und er wirft politische Fragen auf.

spiegel.title: Handball-WM 2027: Bundestrainer Gíslason über Heimvorteil und persönliche Verluste
spiegel.description: Bundestrainer Alfređ Gíslason spricht im Interview über die Chancen der deutschen Handballer bei der Heim-WM, eine umstrittene Auszeit und den Tod enger Vertrauter.

spiegel.title: Essen: Gefangenenbefreiung mit günstigem Fußfesselschlüssel aus dem Netz
spiegel.description: Bei einem Arztbesuch wurde Mitte Oktober in Essen ein Häftling befreit. Dabei, so stellt sich heraus, trug er Fußfesseln, die sich einfach öffnen ließen. Der notwendige Schlüssel ist frei im Internet erhältlich.

nyt.title: Inside Team Trump’s Historic Collapse in the 2026 Midterm Elections
nyt.description: How an unpopular president and an unpopular war provided an opening for Democrats to make sweeping gains in the midterms.

nyt.title: How Trump Is Reacting to the Midterm Results
nyt.description: In the days after Republicans suffered massive midterm election defeats, President Trump appeared unmoved. The New York Times’s White House correspondent Maggie Haberman explains how Trump’s public demeanor compares with what he has shared behind closed doors about voters’ frustration with some of his policies.

nyt.title: They Made History as ‘Firsts.’ That’s Not What They Ran On.
nyt.description: Several midterm winners broke barriers, but with campaigns that focused on delivering material change to the lives of Americans.

nyt.title: ‘Florida Is the Last Main Anchor Standing’ for Republicans
nyt.description: The third most-populous state withstood a national Democratic surge on Tuesday, even as Republicans confronted deep losses in Texas and across the electoral map.

nyt.title: Iran is Reviewing ‘Concrete Proposals’ on Nuclear Program, Officials Say
nyt.description: Iran’s willingness to re-engage on the issue suggests that Qatar-led diplomatic efforts to avert full-blown war between the U.S. and Iran have had some success.

nyt.title: Midterm Election Losses Complicate Trump’s Options on Iran War
nyt.description: The midterm results laid bare the deep unpopularity of the war of choice that President Trump started and is now struggling to end.

nyt.title: Stocks Erase Post-Midterm Elections Rally, Dragged Down by Tech
nyt.description: The S&P 500 slumped to its worst daily decline in more than a year, dragged down by the technology sector as investors fretted about the durability of the A.I. build-out.

nyt.title: Tech Billionaires Face Tricky Political Waters After Democratic Midterm Sweep
nyt.description: Many donated money to President Trump’s favored causes and became his allies. Now that political alignment may be a liability.

nyt.title: At the Root of K-Pop’s Controversies, a Restrictive Business Model
nyt.description: Labels exert extraordinary control over performers because only a few acts turn a profit.

nyt.title: Up in the Clouds With the Pope, It’s Still Commercial
nyt.description: Unlike American presidents, Pope Leo XIV has no private jet, so he travels on commercial airlines, like the rest of us. Well, almost.

nyt.title: Infant Bleeding Surged as Parents Rejected Vitamin K Shots, Studies Find
nyt.description: One study found a 347 percent increase in cases as fewer babies received the shot, which helps blood clot.

nyt.title: He Felt Stuck in New York. So He Started Walking to California.
nyt.description: A Bronx native who’d spent his whole life in the city left on foot in May.

nyt.title: How Melania Trump Became a Dark Horse Diplomat on Ukraine
nyt.description: Both Moscow and Kyiv say Mrs. Trump’s team was the driving force behind an evacuation of a besieged city. It was also in their interest to deliver her a humanitarian win.

nyt.title: Lana Nusseibeh’s U.N. Bid Collides With U.A.E.’s Role in Sudan
nyt.description: Lana Nusseibeh, one of the Gulf nation’s top diplomats, has led the effort to deny her country’s role in Sudan. Now it’s complicating her bid to become secretary general of the United Nations.

nyt.title: Russell Brand Is Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assault
nyt.description: The judge in London said the popular conspiratorial YouTuber and former movie star would be sentenced to “significant custodial time.”

nyt.title: Timeline: How Russell Brand Went From Comedy Star to Convicted Rapist
nyt.description: The comedian, actor and YouTuber has had ups and downs throughout a tumultuous career. A conviction on charges of rape and sexual assault was a new low.

nyt.title: How Did Flávio Bolsonaro Flee Brazil? ‘I’ll Take That to the Grave,’ He Says
nyt.description: From Miami, Flávio Bolsonaro is doubling down on unfounded claims of a stolen election and plotting to sway his nation’s politics from afar, even though his party is not challenging the results.

nyt.title: Bolsonaro’s Escape From Brazil Was Aided by Milei Adviser at Argentine Airport
nyt.description: A top adviser to President Javier Milei of Argentina met Flávio Bolsonaro, the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate, at an Argentine airport, three people involved in the operation said.

elpais.title: Una nueva oleada de falsas amenazas de bomba afecta al menos a 27 aviones con destino a ciudades europeas
elpais.description: Tres aeronaves han tenido origen o destino en Madrid. Bruselas pide colaboración a los Estados para aclarar la incidencia, similar a la registrada el martes en otros siete vuelos

elpais.title: Última hora de la Cumbre Iberoamericana, en directo | Sánchez afirma que la dimisión de Puente fue “por empatía por las víctimas y para restablecer la confianza” en el sistema ferroviario
elpais.description: El presidente, sobre Milei: “El insulto no forma parte de mi forma de hacer política” | Felipe VI: “Somos el contrapunto a un tiempo marcado por los bloques, los frentes y la rivalidad”

elpais.title: Las vidas que se pararon para siempre en Urda
elpais.description: Tras una semana de identificaciones y certificaciones, estas son las víctimas del trágico accidente de tren que ha conmocionado a España

elpais.title: ¿Cómo se están moviendo las encuestas tras el accidente?
elpais.description: EL PAÍS estrena el pódcast ‘Entre datos, con Kiko Llaneras’, analizando los cambios de los sondeos para las elecciones generales del 29N

elpais.title: La UCO registra la casa de Ábalos en Valencia en un nuevo operativo del ‘caso Koldo’ con seis detenidos
elpais.description: El juez Moreno, que abrió este miércoles una pieza secreta tras un informe de la Guardia Civil, autoriza entradas en domicilios de Madrid, Sevilla y Córdoba y pide información a Adif y una constructora

elpais.title: Koldo García asegura que acordó con el abogado del PP un millón de euros a cambio de información para hacer caer a Sánchez
elpais.description: En un audio publicado por la Cadena SER, el exasesor de Ábalos afirma que el letrado le ofreció una rebaja de la pena que suponía no entrar en la cárcel

elpais.title: El Gran Wyoming se jubila y Gonzo presentará ‘El intermedio’ desde enero
elpais.description: El relevo al frente del espacio satírico de La Sexta supondrá la salida de Gonzo de ‘Salvados’, aunque aún no se ha elegido su sustituto

elpais.title: El Asador Etxebarri, elegido el mejor restaurante del mundo
elpais.description: Gaggan, en Bangkok, y Alchemist, en Copenhague, ocupan la segunda y la tercera posición, respectivamente, en la lista de The 50 Best Restaurants 2026. DiverXO cae del cuarto al noveno puesto

elpais.title: Antonia Dell’Atte responde a las disculpas públicas de Ana Obregón: “Te he salvado de una condena y de ir a la cárcel”
elpais.description: La exmodelo italiana ha compartido una publicación en su Instagram en la que dice aceptar el perdón de la presentadora, pero le reprocha haber tardado tanto tiempo: “Después de 35 años, has admitido que has encubierto y defendido a mi maltratador, Alessandro Lecquio”

elpais.title: El canadiense que fue a la Luna abandera un proyecto urbanístico en Madrid con 12.000 viviendas de lujo: “Va a ser algo extraordinario”
elpais.description: El astronauta Jeremy Hansen, que voló en la misión Artemis 2, explica a EL PAÍS su apuesta para una “ciudad inteligente” en torno a una réplica gigante del satélite

elpais.title: Dafne Keen recuerda sus inicios como actriz infantil en ‘Logan’: “Con 11 años me ofrecían cocaína en las fiestas de fin de rodaje”
elpais.description: La intérprete hispanobritánica asegura en un ‘podcast’ que su desinterés por las drogas y el alcohol se debe a los excesos que presenció durante su infancia en Hollywood, y agradece la buena influencia que fue Hugh Jackman para ella: “Era increíblemente protector y maravilloso”

elpais.title: Jueves negro para la Bolsa: el Nasdaq se hunde ante el miedo a que se agudice el frenazo de la IA
elpais.description: El índice bursátil cae un 5% arrastrado por la violenta caída de los fabricantes de chips mientras los inversores temen una ralentización del gasto en tecnología

elpais.title: Tesla y SpaceX pierden 323.000 millones de valor en dos días tras el triunfo demócrata
elpais.description: Los inversores castigan a las compañías de Elon Musk tras la victoria demócrata en Texas y la toma de control del Congreso de Estados Unidos

elpais.title: En mapas: la frontera con México vuelve a los demócratas tras su breve coqueteo con Trump
elpais.description: Los candidatos demócratas ganan o van por delante en todos los distritos de la Cámara de Representantes que son limítrofes con el vecino del sur

elpais.title: Los impuestos, las armas, los derechos de las personas trans y el ‘foie gras’: las otras cuestiones que decidieron las ‘midterms’
elpais.description: Tres de cuatro Estados que llevaron el tema del aborto a las urnas se pronunciaron a favor de garantizar el derecho a la interrupción voluntaria del embarazo

elpais.title: 500.000 gracias
elpais.description: El director de EL PAÍS envía una carta a sus suscriptores para celebrar que ya son medio millón. El diario alcanza este hito en un año muy especial: el de su 50º aniversario

elpais.title: Jan Martínez Ahrens, director de EL PAÍS: “Los suscriptores son la piedra angular del periódico”
elpais.description: El responsable del diario explica en el programa ‘Hoy por hoy’ cómo ha alcanzado el medio millón de personas suscritas en el año de su 50º aniversario

elpais.title: El salario mínimo subirá un 5,3% en 2027, hasta 1.286 euros al mes
elpais.description: La cifra definitiva, ya en audiencia pública y que aprobará en breve el Consejo de Ministros, marca un aumento de 65 euros, cinco más que la propuesta de los expertos

npr.title: Russell Brand is convicted of rape, and judge says he'll get a prison term
npr.description: A prosecutor described Brand as a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator." Brand, 51, denied the charges, saying he had never forced anyone to do something against their will.

npr.title: What's next for Democrats after the midterms. And, a look at the outstanding races
npr.description: Democrats have regained control of Congress. They have a long list of investigations into Trump planned. And, not all races have been called. Here's a look at how they could affect the Dems' majority.

npr.title: Bob Dylan comes knockin' on pope's door as Leo welcomes legend to Vatican
npr.description: The American singer-songwriter and poet visited with the American pope at the Vatican during a break between concert dates in Italy. The Vatican said the encounter was brief.

npr.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison
npr.description: Wong was sentenced for his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed national security law, in a case that critics say reflects the crackdown on the city's once-thriving pro-democracy movement.

npr.title: Abdul El-Sayed welcomes Trump's plan to cut Israel aid, calls for end to arms sales
npr.description: Michigan's first Muslim senator-elect, Abdul El-Sayed, discusses his historic victory, an unlikely agreement with Trump on Israel military aid and the political divisions that remain.

npr.title: The world is reacting to the Democrats' sweeping midterm elections victory
npr.description: From Kyiv to Moscow, and Tehran to Tel Aviv, all eyes were on the Democrats' big win as foreign powers weigh how a flipped Congress will affect international relations.

npr.title: Democrats seize full control of Congress. And, which candidates made history last night
npr.description: Democrats have won the House and the Senate, taking full control of Congress for the first time since 2023. And history was made in several states. Here's what happened last night.

npr.title: Japan faces diplomatic dilemma amid joint pressure from nuclear neighbors
npr.description: As the Ukraine war grinds on, ties between Russia and neighboring Japan are at their worst in decades. Tokyo wants more support from Washington, but some Japanese are concerned they may not get it.

npr.title: For Ukraine's Kherson region, a short ceasefire meant a momentary return to normal life
npr.description: In Kherson city, usually seething with Russian drones, friends met at cafes, families were out together and shoppers stocked up. "The city seems alive," said one resident, "just like it used to be."

npr.title: Indian navy rescues 20 crew from Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia
npr.description: he operation involved a warship, a maritime surveillance aircraft and marine commandos. The hijacking followed a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean.

republika.title: Fine vita, il governo impugna la legge del Veneto. Calderoli contrario, Salvini diserta
republika.description: La regione amministrata dal leghista Stefani era stata la prima di centrodestra a dare il via libera al suicidio assistito

republika.title: Via al nuovo Report tra lacrime e orgoglio: “Speriamo che Ranucci faccia il tifo per noi”
republika.description: La conferenza stampa di lancio della trasmissione che prova a voltare pagina dopo le polemiche per il caso Lavitola. Corsini: “La mia verifica è il terminale di una catena. Spero d’ora in poi in modo leggermente più comodo”

republika.title: Paola, violentata e minacciata di morte: “Mi sentivo sporca ma ora dico a tutte: non vergognatevi”
republika.description: Ha 55 anni, fa l’operatrice sociosanitaria e nell’agosto del 2025 fu stuprata sul percorso natura di San Damaso a Modena. Dopo la condanna a 15 anni di un ventenne, ha deciso di parlare. “Nessuno deve più subire quello che ho subito io”

republika.title: Violentarono una studentessa dopo la promozione del Bra, tre calciatori condannati
republika.description: Il tribunale di Asti ha inflitto 4 anni e 2 mesi a Fausto Perseu e Alessio Rosa, e 3 anni 8 mesi e 20 giorni a Jesus Christ Mawete: approfittarono delle condizioni di stordimento da alcol della giovane per consumare uno stupro di gruppo

republika.title: Incubo Paraguay, mezzo Paese si sveglia senza più soldi in banca. Il presidente si dimette
republika.description: Bloccati conti e carte, impossibile ritirare i soldi o effettuare pagamenti a causa del crac della Ueno. C’è chi potrebbe aver perso tutto. Il passo indietro di Peña, che rischiava l’impeachment

republika.title: Omicidi di Villa Pamphili, Francis Kaufman condannato all’ergastolo. “Sentenza giusta”
republika.description: Il verdetto dei giudici della prima Corte di Assise di Roma. Disposto l’isolamento diurno per tre anni. Soddisfatte le parti civili. La difesa: “Manca la prova regina”

republika.title: Così la Difesa italiana si sta preparando alla guerra al tempo dei droni
republika.description: Inutile riempire i magazzini di quadricotteri, obsoleti dopo pochi mesi. La strategia dell’Esercito è addestrare subito tanti piloti e prendere i sistemi in massa solo nel momento di necessità. Una sfida anche per l’industria

republika.title: Regno Unito, Russell Brand giudicato colpevole per uno stupro e tre aggressioni sessuali
republika.description: Il verdetto di colpevolezza per accuse risalenti a oltre 20 anni fa. All’attore sarà inflitta la detenzione in prigione, l’entità della pena sarà determinata in sentenza successivamente

republika.title: Elezioni midterm Usa, le news in diretta. Trump: “Ricevute lamentele su Hegseth, ma rimane”
republika.description: A meno di 48 ore dalla sconfitta elettorale alle elezioni di metà mandato i rep puntano il dito contro il capo del Pentagono. Rubio valuta dimissioni per prendere le distanze da Trump e guardare al 2028. Continua lo spoglio in Alaska e Mississipi

republika.title: L’effetto giovani sul voto e le risposte di Meloni. Ecco perché per i ventenni ci sono solo briciole
republika.description: Gli elettori tra i 18 e i 34 anni hanno trainato l’affluenza alle urne sulla separazione delle carriere a favore del No. Senza trascurare la spinta di ventenni e trentenni nell’ondata che ha travolto Donald Trump

The pair decays into a muon and antimuon, which are particles similar to electrons. Because evidence for this decay helps test theoretical predictions from the Standard Model, physicists have been waiting for it since 1984, when it was first theorized.

phys-org.description: In 2018, something strange happened on sidewalks across America. In 65 cities, thousands of electric scooters appeared seemingly overnight, often with little or no advance notice to local governments. Cease-and-desist orders flew. Scooters were impounded. Even after cities imposed regulations, there seemed to be far more scooters than anyone could ever use.

phys-org.description: A new study has revealed how the repurposing of an ancestral gene saved the embryos of cod's ancestors from extinction, enabling them to form the large populations that, millions of years later, would change the course of human history. The codfishes and their relatives in the order Gadiformes lost genes essential for egg buoyancy and the survival of their embryos, yet survived by adaptively recruiting mechanisms that aid egg ovulation in freshwater fishes.

phys-org.title: When Einstein's gravitational waves meet Newton's tides

In a new study, a mathematician at Freie Universität Berlin has outlined how a targeted approach could be used to search for effects of this nature.

phys-org.title: NASA's Swift telescope has burned up, months after a robot sent to save it failed

NASA ended the telescope's mission three days later, because Swift had sunk so low that drag from the thin air there meant its telescopes couldn't hold steady.

The collision left Earth spinning extremely fast, with days lasting just two to five hours. Yet existing models of how Earth's first crust formed and evolved have largely overlooked how the planet's later slowdown might have affected it.

The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors

They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?

But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

proj-syn.title: Why Are Indian Protesters Targeting the Electoral Commission?
proj-syn.description: Following a “special intensive revision” that struck 130 million voters from the electoral rolls, India’s youth have mounted large-scale protests against the Election Commission. Given the convergence of protests with the formal political opposition, the Commission is unlikely to avoid accountability for mass disenfranchisement.

proj-syn.title: Why Aren’t We Investing More in Climate Adaptation?
proj-syn.description: There are many proven ways to protect people and assets from extreme weather, and such measures often prevent economic losses worth many times their cost. But ensuring their implementation requires making them more affordable and creating innovative revenue mechanisms and financing structures.

proj-syn.title: Put the Ocean at the Center of COP31
proj-syn.description: Last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Belém, Brazil, put forests high on the climate agenda. This month’s UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, can do the same for the ocean, whose warming threatens not just food and energy security but global survival.

proj-syn.title: Who's Winning (and Who's Losing) The Ocean?
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Peter Thomson, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Ocean, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as he warns of a “world on fire,” takes governments to task for kowtowing to the oil and gas industry, and explains how we can do better for future generations.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats’ Historic Duty
proj-syn.description: While Democrats have good reason to celebrate their historic midterm victory, their current elation must quickly harden into determination. Fortunately, the field for new ideas, systemic and economic, in the US will be the most open it is likely to be for decades.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.

proj-syn.title: Good Institutions Require Good People
proj-syn.description: Well-designed laws, courts, catechisms, extrinsic motives, social approval, and even a few good and decent people are of no avail if too many people do not behave like self-respecting and other-respecting adults. Childish pride and envy, grabbing more of the sweets, Donald Trump-style, do not make for a good society.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchic World Order
proj-syn.description: Today, some 64 heads of state or government are oligarchs, leading countries that together account for some 60% of global GDP. The question is thus no longer whether oligarchs will rule the world, but rather what kind of world they are building.

proj-syn.title: Poland’s Constitutional Civil War
proj-syn.description: Polish right-wing populists recently stormed the country's Constitutional Tribunal, winning applause from the Kremlin and far-right fellow-travelers across Europe. As in other countries, the constitutional tribunal is the institution that distinguishes a proper democracy from a dictatorship making it a target for authoritarians.

proj-syn.title: The Tech Brotherhood Wants Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: After centuries of nation-states, a new form of sovereignty is asserting itself. The small fraternity that controls the major digital platforms has already proven capable of even more intrusive and insidious forms of control than most states can muster.

proj-syn.title: The Far Right’s Vision for Europe
proj-syn.description: In many ways, Europe’s far right has already won, regardless of what happens at the ballot box in the coming months. Its parties may still quarrel among themselves, but they agree on the three big issues that will define much of the European political agenda for years to come.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Bright Future
proj-syn.description: A narrative of European decline has taken hold, and if the EU continues on its current path, it may well materialize. But this is not a foregone conclusion: Europe retains considerable strengths on which it can build as it pursues critical reforms aimed at unleashing innovation.

proj-syn.title: A Debtors’ Club for a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: The newly created Borrowers’ Platform aims to facilitate knowledge-sharing and capacity-building among debtor countries, while amplifying their voices in global financial circles. But at a time when the Paris Club of sovereign creditors is increasingly unable to act collectively, the Borrowers’ Platform should ramp up its ambition.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Tariff Fiasco Could Save Free Trade
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s tariffs have raised prices and hurt businesses without reducing the trade deficit or creating manufacturing jobs. But global trade has held up better than expected, and growing public opposition to tariffs could pave the way for a retreat from protectionism.
